D5 V2 Manual HTO Demux

see D3 for notes

```{r echo = T, results = 'hide'}
Sys.setenv("DISPLAY"=":0")
library(dplyr)
library(Seurat)
library(data.table)
```
```{r}
# Load the DC D5 RNA dataset
d5.data <- Read10X(data.dir = "../rna_d5/outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/")
# 8515 cells
# Initialize the Seurat object with the raw (non-normalized data).
d5 <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = d5.data, project = "DC", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)
# 8483 cells
```

```{r}
# The [[ operator can add columns to object metadata. This is a great place to stash QC stats
d5[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(d5, pattern = "^mt-")
```

```{r}
# Visualize QC metrics as a violin plot
VlnPlot(d5, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"), ncol = 3, pt.size = 0.01, log = TRUE)
```
```{r}
# FeatureScatter is typically used to visualize feature-feature relationships, but can be used
# for anything calculated by the object, i.e. columns in object metadata, PC scores etc.

plot1 <- FeatureScatter(d5, feature1 = "nFeature_RNA", feature2 = "percent.mt", pt.size = 0.1)
plot2 <- FeatureScatter(d5, feature1 = "nFeature_RNA", feature2 = "nCount_RNA", pt.size = 0.1)
CombinePlots(plots = list(plot1, plot2))
```

```{r}
# exclude high Mito cells
d5 <- subset(d5, subset = percent.mt < 10)
plot1 <- FeatureScatter(d5, feature1 = "nFeature_RNA", feature2 = "percent.mt", pt.size = 0.1)
plot2 <- FeatureScatter(d5, feature1 = "nFeature_RNA", feature2 = "nCount_RNA", pt.size = 0.1)
CombinePlots(plots = list(plot1, plot2))
# 7531 cells <10
```

```{r}
scrub <- read.table("scrublet_d5.csv", sep=",", header=TRUE)
d5 <- AddMetaData(
  object = d5,
  metadata = scrub$doublet_score,
  col.name = 'scrubScore'
)
d5 <- AddMetaData(
  object = d5,
  metadata = scrub$predicted_doublet,
  col.name = 'scrubCall'
)
plot1 <- FeatureScatter(d5, feature1 = "nFeature_RNA", feature2 = "percent.mt", pt.size = 0.1)
plot2 <- FeatureScatter(d5, feature1 = "scrubScore", feature2 = "percent.mt", pt.size = 0.1)
CombinePlots(plots = list(plot1, plot2))
```

```{r}
d5 <- subset(d5, subset = scrubCall == 'False') #7440 cells
```

```{r}
d5Hto <- Read10X(data.dir = "../citeseq/d5HtoCount/umi_count/", gene.column = 1)
#Save only 2 meaningful hashtags
d5Hto <- d5Hto[c(3,5),]
rownames(d5Hto) <- substring(rownames(d5Hto), 1, 5)
# Select cell barcodes detected by both RNA and HTO In the example datasets we have already
joint.bcs <- intersect(colnames(d5), colnames(d5Hto))
# Subset RNA and HTO counts by joint cell barcodes
d5 <- d5[, joint.bcs]  #7438 cells
d5Hto <- d5Hto[, joint.bcs]

# Confirm that the HTO have the correct names
rownames(d5Hto)

# Add HTO data as a new assay independent from RNA
d5[["HTO"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = d5Hto)
# Normalize HTO data, here we use centered log-ratio (CLR) transformation
d5 <- NormalizeData(d5, assay = "HTO", normalization.method = "CLR")

FeatureScatter(d5, feature1 = "Hash3", feature2 = "Hash5")
```
```{r}
### manual Demux, no need compensation
d5temp <- d5
FeatureScatter(d5temp, feature1 = "Hash3", feature2= "Hash5")
d5temp1 <- subset(d5temp, hto_Hash5 >= 0.6)
hist(d5temp1@assays$HTO@data[1,],breaks =50) #Hash3 >0.6
d5temp2 <- subset(d5temp, hto_Hash3 >= 0.6)
hist(d5temp2@assays$HTO@data[2,],breaks =50) #Hash5 >0.6
d5temp <- subset(d5temp, ( hto_Hash3>0.6) & (hto_Hash5>0.6), invert = TRUE)
d5temp <- subset(d5temp, ( hto_Hash3<0.4) & (hto_Hash5<0.4), invert = TRUE)

## Test HTODemux() View doublet call
d5temp3 <- HTODemux(d5temp, assay = "HTO", positive.quantile = 0.99, init = 2)
Idents(d5temp3) <- "HTO_classification.global"
FeatureScatter(d5temp3, feature1 = "Hash3", feature2 = "Hash5")

## Demux with filtered data
d5temp <- HTODemux(d5temp, assay = "HTO", positive.quantile = 0.99, init = 2)

d5 <- d5temp # 7182 cells
# Global classification results
table(d5$HTO_classification.global)
# Group cells based on the max HTO signal
Idents(d5) <- "HTO_maxID"
RidgePlot(d5, assay = "HTO", features = rownames(d5[["HTO"]])[1:2], ncol = 1)
FeatureScatter(d5, feature1 = "Hash3", feature2 = "Hash5")
```

```{r}
## No need to run doublet or negative this time. All ready excluded by manual
## Calculate a distance matrix using HTO
## not useful for 2 hashtags
## To increase the efficiency of plotting, you can subsample cells using the num.cells argument
```

```{r}
# Extract the singlets, no need this round.
# d3 <- subset(d3, idents = "Doublet", invert = TRUE)
d5 <- NormalizeData(d5)
# Select the top 1000 most variable features
d5 <- FindVariableFeatures(d5, selection.method = "mean.var.plot")

# Scaling RNA data, we only scale the variable features here for efficiency
d5 <- ScaleData(d5, features = VariableFeatures(d5))

# Run PCA
d5 <- RunPCA(d5, features = VariableFeatures(d5))

## Store in d5temp here
# d5temp <- d5 #968.5Mb

#View PCA
VizDimLoadings(d5, dims = 1:4, reduction = "pca")

## In particular DimHeatmap allows for easy exploration of the primary sources of heterogeneity in a dataset, and can be useful when trying to decide which PCs to include for further downstream analyses. Both cells and features are ordered according to their PCA scores. Setting cells to a number plots the ‘extreme’ cells on both ends of the spectrum, which dramatically speeds plotting for large datasets. Though clearly a supervised analysis, we find this to be a valuable tool for exploring correlated feature sets.

DimHeatmap(d5, dims = 1:15, cells = 500, balanced = TRUE)
```

```{r}
## Determine the ‘dimensionality’ of the dataset
# JackStraw procedure
d5 <- JackStraw(d5, num.replicate = 100, dims = 50)
d5 <- ScoreJackStraw(d5, dims = 1:40)

# 'Significant' PCs will show a strong enrichment of features with low p-values (solid curve above the dashed line). 
JackStrawPlot(d5, dims = 1:40)

```
```{r}
ElbowPlot(d5, ndims = 40)
```

```{r}
# to restore d5
#d5 <- d5temp  
# We select the top 10 PCs for clustering and tSNE based on PCElbowPlot
d5 <- FindNeighbors(d5, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:29)
d5 <- FindClusters(d5, resolution = 2, verbose = FALSE)
d5 <- RunTSNE(d5, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:20)

# Projecting singlet identities on TSNE visualization
DimPlot(d5, group.by = "HTO_maxID")
```

FeaturePlot(d5, features = "Siglech", split.by = "HTO_maxID")

```{r}
d5Adt <- Read10X(data.dir = "../citeseq/d5AdtCount/umi_count/", gene.column = 1)
d5Adt <- d5Adt[1:9,]
rownames(d5Adt) <- gsub('.{16}$', '', rownames(d5Adt))
rownames(d5Adt) <- paste0('Adt.', rownames(d5Adt))
joint.bcs <- intersect(colnames(d5), colnames(d5Adt))
d5Adt <- d5Adt[, joint.bcs]
d5 <- d5[, joint.bcs]
d5[["ADT"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = d5Adt)
d5 <- NormalizeData(d5, assay = "ADT", normalization.method = "CLR")
d5 <- ScaleData(d5, assay = "ADT")
RidgePlot(d5, features = c("Adt.CD11c", "Adt.CD11b", "Adt.B220",  "Adt.Gr1",   "Adt.MHCII", "Adt.SiglecH", "Adt.Sirpa", "Adt.CD24",  "Adt.F480"), ncol = 2)
```
